title: Lessons
summary: The unit of learning: one job each, one type from a flat list, its own schedule and mastery.
description:
Learning happens in lessons. Every lesson has one type, and the type says everything about it: how it is practised, what its page shows, where it goes in a course and what mastering it takes. There are two ways a lesson runs: a drill is a run of exercises tapped through; a conversation is an exchange with an examiner or a writing partner that ends in a verdict.

A lesson owns what it practises. A word or a sentence belongs to exactly one lesson.

requirements.text: Every lesson has exactly one type from the registry: words, pictures, scene, story, typing, memory, sentences, gaps, dialogue, study, listening or writing.

Each type is declared once, with its name, icon, description, how it runs, its place in a course's path and the sections its page shows; the screens draw a lesson from its registry entry, not from its type.
A drill owns its words, sentences or dialogue lines; a study lesson owns its text and objectives.
A word or sentence belongs to exactly one lesson.
Every lesson has a complexity of low, medium or high (shown as quick, medium, deep), which says how long it takes and how deep it goes, not its level.
A lesson's minutes come from one table: drills 2, 4 and 8 for low, medium and high; conversations 5, 10 and 20.
A lesson can carry its own CEFR level; without one it has its course's.
A lesson can be marked a challenge: it does not count toward completing its course, and the daily list offers it only once the course's other lessons are passed.
A lesson already passed today can be practised again at any time as extra practice.
A new lesson type added to the registry is described to the tutor automatically, from its registry entry.
Every registered type can be made and practised, and every exercise it produces is one the screens can draw; a test fails otherwise.

questions: The principle says nothing else branches on a lesson's type, but the core still names types in a few places: cutting a course's items into drills, drawing a picture lesson's words, and a check for writing in the tutor. Are those exceptions accepted, or should they move into the types?
